Rashi on Yevamot 18b:10:1.english: With a single brother - For certainly, by virtue of the levirate bond of this [brother] who was not in his world, she is forbidden to this [brother] to be taken in levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:10:2.hebrew: אי נמי בתרי - אחים, ומת האחד, ונולד להם אח השלישי:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:10:2.english: Alternatively, in [the case of] two - brothers, and one died, and a third brother was born to them.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:10:3.english: And he did not perform levirate marriage - This second [brother did not take] his sister-in-law [in levirate marriage].

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:10:4.hebrew: ולא מת - אסורה לזה שנולד לאחר מיתה ליבמה, מזיקת אח שלא היה בעולמו. אבל היכא דייבמה השני, פקעה זיקת אח הראשון ונעשית אשתו של זה השני. אי נמי לא יבמה האי שני, הואיל והוזקקה לו, הרי היא ככנוסה כדלקמן, וכשמת, מותרת לשלישי:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:10:4.english: And did not die - She is forbidden to this [brother] who was born after [the first brother's] death to take her in levirate marriage, due to the levirate bond of a brother with whom he did not coexist. However, where the second [brother] took her in levirate marriage, the levirate bond of the first brother has departed, and she has become the wife of this second [brother]. Alternatively, [even if] this second [brother] did not take her in levirate marriage, since she became bound to him [for levirate marriage], she is as though married [to him], as [explained] below, and when he dies, she is permitted to the third [brother].

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:11:1.hebrew: בהתירא אשכחה - שלא נאסרה עליו שעה אחת, שלא נזקקה לו מכח הראשון כלום:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:11:1.english: He found her in a permitted [state] - For she was not forbidden to him for a single hour, since she was not bound to him by virtue of the first [brother] at all.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:11:2.hebrew: יש זיקה - כשנפלה לפני השני קודם לידתו של זה ונזקקה לו, לשני, אלימא ההיא זיקה לשוויא ככנוסה, והוי ליה כייבם ולבסוף נולד:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:11:2.english: There is a levirate bond - When she fell before the second [brother] before the birth of this [brother] and became bound to him, to the second [brother], that levirate bond is strong [enough] to render her like a married woman, and it is [considered] like [a case where] he performed levirate marriage and subsequently [the brother] was born.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:14:1.hebrew: זיקת יבם אחד - כגון שלא נפלה אלא פעם אחת, או שכנסה שני ופקעה זיקה ראשונה, וכשמת אין כאן אלא זיקת ייבום של שני, או לא עשה בה מאמר ומת, אין כאן אלא זיקת ייבום ראשון. ועכשיו יש כאן זיקת ייבום של שני יבמין, שיש עליה קצת זיקה מן הראשון, דכל זמן שלא נתייבמה לא פקע, ויש עליה זיקתה מן השני; וצרתה, אשת השני, אסורה משום דידה:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:14:1.english: The bond of a single yavam - For example, where she fell [for levirate marriage] only once; or where the second [brother] married her and the first bond expired, so that when he died there is only the levirate bond of the second; or [where the second] did not perform ma'amar [levirate betrothal] with her and died, [so] there is only the levirate bond of the first. But now there is a levirate bond of two yevamin, for she has a partial bond from the first [brother], since as long as she has not been taken in levirate marriage it has not expired, and [she also has] her bond from the second; and her rival wife — the wife of the second [brother] — is forbidden because of her.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:15:1.hebrew: מייבם לאיזו שירצה - דלית ליה הך דרשה דזיקת שני יבמים. דאי מאמר קונה, הרי היא אשת שני ואין כאן אלא זיקתו; ואם אין קונה, הרי הוא כמו שאינו, ואין כאן אלא זיקת ראשון:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:15:1.english: He performs levirate marriage with whichever [one] he wishes - For he does not accept this exposition regarding the levirate bond of two yevamim. For if ma'amar acquires [her], behold, she is the wife of the second [brother], and there is only his levirate bond here; and if it does not acquire [her], behold, it is as though it does not exist, and there is only the levirate bond of the first [brother] here.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:15:2.english: And performs chalitzah with the second - Because of [the] doubt, as [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:1:1.english: A woman waiting for a yavam - [She is] waiting for her yavam [to perform] levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:1:2.english: Whose brother betrothed - [The brother] of the yavam [betrothed] her sister after this [woman] fell before him.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:1:3.hebrew: אומרים לו - למארס, המתן מלכנוס, לפי שאחות זקוקתו היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:1:3.english: They say to him - To the one who betrothed [her]: Wait before marrying [her], because she is the sister of the woman bound to him [by the levirate bond].

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:1:4.english: Until your brother performs an action - Until your brother performs levirate marriage with the yevamah and her levirate bond with you is dissolved. Evidently, a levirate bond forbids her sister.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:1.hebrew: א"ל - רב יוסף לאביי, ואי משמיה דרב אמרה, מאי קשיא לך:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:1.english: He said to him - Rav Yosef [said] to Abaye: And if he stated it in the name of Rav, what is your difficulty?

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:2.hebrew: דרב אדרב - דא"ר הונא אמר רב לעיל, מותר באמה:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:2.english: Of Rav against Rav - For Rav Huna said [that] Rav said earlier: he is permitted [to marry] her mother.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:3.english: They are amora'im - Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda were disciples of Rav, and they disagree regarding his [opinion]:

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:4.hebrew: כיון דאיתמר משמיה דשמואל בהדיא - דיש זיקה, דשמואל עצמו אמרה ולא תלמידו משמו, ומצינו למימר דרב יהודה תלמידו מכלל אותה שמועה אמר לההיא דידיה:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:4.english: Since it was stated in the name of Shmuel explicitly - that there is a levirate bond, for Shmuel himself said it and not his student in his name; and we can say that Rav Yehuda, his student, stated that [statement] of his by inference from that teaching.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:5.hebrew: ומשמיה דרב איתמר כאמוראי - בפלוגתא, דהא פליג רב הונא. לא שבקינן כו':
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:2:5.english: And in the name of Rav it was stated as [a dispute between] Amoraim - In a dispute, for Rav Huna disagrees. "We do not leave," etc.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:3:1.hebrew: הכי קמתניתו לה - לרב יהודה דלעיל בסתמא, שלא הזכיר שם רבו, וצריכיתו למידק הא דרב יהודה דשמואל היא:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:3:1.english: This is how you teach it - [You teach the statement of] Rav Yehuda above anonymously, without mentioning the name of his teacher, and you must infer [that] this [statement] of Rav Yehuda is [in the name] of Shmuel.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:3:2.hebrew: <abbr title="הכי גרסינן">ה"ג</abbr>: אנן בהדיא מתנינן לה:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:3:2.english: This is the reading: "We teach it explicitly."

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:3:3.english: And Shmuel follows his [own] reasoning - Rav Kahana said all of it.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:4:1.hebrew: ה"מ מחיים - כל זמן שיבמתו קיימת:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:4:1.english: This applies while [she is] living - As long as his yevamah is alive.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:5:1.english: And he died - The one who performed levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:6:1.hebrew: מייבם לאיזו שירצה - ופטורה חברתה. ולאו אעשה בה מאמר קאי, אלא ארישא דקתני הראשונה יוצאה כו', דקאמר ר"ש דכיון דכשנולד כבר נתייבמה, ולא היתה על זה בזיקת נישואי אחיו הראשון מעולם, מותרת לו:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:6:1.english: He enters into levirate marriage with whichever [one] he wishes - And her co-wife is exempt. And [Rabbi Shimon] is not referring to [the case where] he performed ma'amar with her, but rather to the first clause [of the Mishnah], which teaches: "The first one leaves, etc." — regarding which Rabbi Shimon says that since when [the third brother] was born she had already been taken in levirate marriage, and she was never [bound] to this [brother] by the levirate bond of his first brother's marriage, she is permitted to him.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:7:1.hebrew: אף בראשונה - וקא שרי נולד ואח"כ ייבם:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:7:1.english: Even on the first [Mishnah] - And [Rabbi Shimon] permits [the case where the third brother] was born and afterward [the second brother] performed levirate marriage.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:7:2.hebrew: מדקתני משנה יתירה - לכולה ההיא בבא דרישא, דלמאן קתני לה אי לאו דפלוגתא דר"ש עלה קיימא? ולהכי תנייה לאשמועינן דאפי' בההיא שרי:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:7:2.english: From [the fact] that it teaches a superfluous Mishnah - [this refers] to that entire clause of the first [Mishnah], for whom does it teach it if not that Rabbi Shimon's dispute applies to it? And for this [reason] it taught it, to inform us that even in that [case] he permits [it].

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:8:1.english: For whom does it teach it - To teach us whose ruling it was necessary [to state].

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:8:2.hebrew: אילימא לרבנן - לאשמועינן איסורא לרבנן, דהא לא איסור ולא היתר לר"ש שמעת מינה ברישא, דהא לא איירי בה:
Rashi on Yevamot 18b:8:2.english: If we say [it is] according to the Rabbis - [That is, it was taught] to teach us the prohibition according to the Rabbis, for you do not learn either prohibition or permission for Rabbi Shimon from it in the first clause, since it does not deal with it.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:9:1.english: And he waited for them - He waited for them.

Rashi on Yevamot 18b:9:2.english: And then he disagreed with them - Regarding the entire matter.

Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:10:1.hebrew: משכחת לה בחד אחא - וא"ת: לעיל בפ"ק (יבמות דף ט: ושם) בשמעתיה דלוי קאמר "בפלוגתא לא קמיירי", ופריך: "והא א"ר אושעיא חלוק היה ר"ש אף בראשונה" — הא לרבי אושעיא נמי משכחת לה בחד אחא, ולפטור צרתה וצרת צרתה נמי משכחת לה למאי דאמר לקמן דמודי ר"ש בזיקת שני יבמין דלאו ככנוסה דמיא? וי"ל: דמתני' דפרקין אתא לפרושי פרקין קמא, דקתני "כיצד אשת אחיו שלא הי' בעולמו"; ולר' אושעיה דחלוק ר"ש אף בראשונה, ע"כ מתני' דפרק קמא איירי בפלוגתא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:10:1.english: You can find it in [the case of] a single brother - And if you ask: Above in the first chapter (Yevamot 9b, and elsewhere), in the discussion of Levi, [the Gemara] says, "He does not teach [a case that is subject to] a dispute," and [the Gemara] challenges, "But Rabbi Oshaya said: Rabbi Shimon disagreed even with regard to the first [case]!" — [Why is that a difficulty?] Even according to Rabbi Oshaya, you can find it in [the case of] a single brother, and you can also find [a case] to exempt her co-wife and her co-wife's co-wife, according to what [the Gemara] says below that Rabbi Shimon agrees regarding the levirate bond of two levirs that she is not considered like a married woman! And one can answer: The Mishnah of our chapter comes to explain our first chapter, as it teaches, "How [is the case of] the wife of his brother who was not in his world?" And according to Rabbi Oshaya, that Rabbi Shimon disagrees even with regard to the first [case], perforce the Mishnah of the first chapter is dealing with a dispute.

Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:1:1.hebrew: שומרת יבם שקידש אחיו את אחותה כו' - אר"י דדוקא קידש, אומרים לו המתן מלישא, משום דבשעת נישואין נראה כנושא אחות זקוקתו; אבל אם נשא כבר, שהיא אשתו גמורה — פקע לה זיקה לגמרי, ואין צריך להמתין מלבעול. ודוקא קידש אחר נפילה, כדמוכח בהחולץ (לקמן יבמות מא. ושם), דבקידש באיסור איירי; דמסיק עלה: מתה אשתו — מותר ביבמתו, משום דהואי יבמה שהותרה ונאסרה וחזרה והותרה. אבל אם קידש בהיתר קודם נפילה, שלא היתה אחות זקוקתו בשעת קידושין — א"צ להמתין כלל:
Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:1:1.english: A widow waiting for her yavam, [if] his brother betrothed her sister, etc. - R. Yitzchak said that specifically [where] he betrothed [her], they say to him, "Wait" from marrying [her], because at the time of marriage he appears as one who marries the sister of a woman bound to him [by the levirate bond]. However, if he already married [her], such that she is his full wife, the levirate bond has completely lapsed, and he does not need to wait before cohabiting [with her]. And specifically [this applies where] he betrothed [her] after [the widow] fell [for levirate marriage], as is proven in [the chapter] HaCholetz (below, Yevamot 41a and there), for it is speaking of [a case] where he betrothed [her] under a prohibition; as [the Gemara] concludes regarding it: [If] his wife died, he is permitted to [marry] his yevamah, because she was a yevamah who was permitted, then forbidden, and then permitted again. However, if he betrothed [her] permissibly before [the widow] fell [for levirate marriage], when she was not the sister of a woman bound to him at the time of betrothal, he does not need to wait at all:

Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:1:2.hebrew: אומרים לו המתן - וא"ת: למה צריך להמתין? דכיון דקדשה, פקעה לה זיקה לגמרי, כדמוכח בפ' ד' אחים (לקמן יבמות כט. ושם) גבי הא דא"ר אלעזר: מאמר לב"ש אינו קונה קנין גמור אלא לדחות בצרה בלבד; א"ר אבין: אף אנן נמי תנינא: ב"ש אומר יקיימו — דיעבד אין, לכתחלה לא; ואי ס"ד דמאמר קונה קנין גמור, זה יעשה מאמר ויקנה וזה יעשה מאמר ויקנה. ומאי קושיא? אפי' קני קנין גמור, הא אמרי' הכא דצריך להמתין בקידושין דאורייתא! — ולפי מאי דפרישית לעיל דמש"ה חשיב לר"י בן בתירה יחידאה, א"ש. וי"ל: דלר"י בן בתירה דסבר יש זיקה, אין הקידושין מפקיעים הזיקה; אבל ר' אבין סבר אין זיקה, ולא אסור לייבם אלא משום ביטול מצות יבמין, ולהכי פריך: אי מאמר קונה לב"ש קנין גמור, זה יעשה קנין גמור ויקנה וזה יעשה מאמר ויקנה — ויכולים לעשות ע"י שליח בבת אחת, דליכא ביטול מצות יבמין. והא דשרי הכא לקיימה אפי' לרבי יהודה בן בתירה, ובפ' ד' אחין ששניהם נשואים ב' אחיות דאייתי לעיל קתני סיפא "קדמו וכנסו יוציאו" — אר"י: דשאני גבי ד' אחים, שהאחיות לא היו באות לעולם לכלל היתר, שכל אחת אחות זקוקתו; אבל היכא דאחות יבמה אתיא לכלל היתר לאחר שיעשה אחיו מעשה, לא החמירו להוציא:
Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:1:2.english: "They say to him: Wait" - And if you ask: Why must he wait? For once he has betrothed her, the levirate bond is completely dissolved, as is proven in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim (below, Yevamot 29a and there) regarding that which Rabbi Elazar said: Ma'amar according to Beit Shammai does not effect a complete acquisition, but only [serves] to push aside the rival wife; Rabbi Avin said: We too have learned [this in a Mishnah]: Beit Shammai say they may keep [them] — [meaning] after the fact, yes, [but] ab initio, no; and if it should enter your mind that ma'amar effects a complete acquisition, this one should perform ma'amar and acquire [his yevamah] and that one should perform ma'amar and acquire [his yevamah]. And what is the difficulty? Even if [ma'amar] effects a complete acquisition, behold we say here that one must wait [even] with biblical betrothal! — And according to what I explained above, that for this reason Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira is considered an individual opinion, it is well. And one can answer: According to Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, who holds that there is a [substantial] levirate bond, betrothal does not dissolve the levirate bond; whereas Rabbi Avin holds that there is no [substantial] levirate bond, and it is forbidden to perform levirate marriage only because of [the prohibition against] nullifying the mitzvah of yevamim, and therefore he asks: If ma'amar according to Beit Shammai effects a complete acquisition, this one should effect a complete acquisition and acquire [her] and that one should perform ma'amar and acquire [her] — and they can do so simultaneously via an agent, so that there is no nullification of the mitzvah of yevamim. And [as for] that which [the Mishnah] permits here to keep her even according to Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira, whereas in the chapter [entitled] Arba'ah Achim, [where] two [brothers] are married to two sisters, which [the Gemara] cited above, the latter clause teaches "if they went ahead and married [them], they must divorce [them]" — Rabbi Yitzchak said: [The case of] Arba'ah Achim is different, because the sisters would never have come into a state of permissibility, since each one is the sister of his zekukah; whereas where the sister of a yevamah will come into a state of permissibility after his brother performs an action, [the Sages] were not stringent [to require him] to divorce [her].

Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:2:1.hebrew: דאי דרב מאי - וא"ת: דבסוף פ"ק דכתובות (דף יב:) נמי אמרינן "הא דרב יהודה דשמואל היא", ולא פריך "דאי דרב מאי"? וי"ל: דהכא משמע דרב יהודה משמיה דרב קאמר לה, דקאי ארב הונא דקאמר משמיה דרב: שומרת יבם שמתה — מותר באמה:
Tosafot on Yevamot 18b:2:1.english: And if [it were the opinion] of Rav, what [problem would there be]? - And if you ask: at the end of the first chapter of Ketubot (12b), we also say, "This [statement] of Rav Yehudah is [the view] of Shmuel," and [the Gemara there] does not ask, "And if [it were the view] of Rav, what [problem would there be]?" And one can answer: here it sounds as if Rav Yehudah said it in the name of Rav, because he is referring to Rav Huna, who said in the name of Rav: [Regarding] a shomeret yavam [a woman awaiting levirate marriage] who died — he [the yavam] is permitted to [marry] her mother.
